# COLRv1 renderer fixtures

`test_glyphs-glyf_colr_1_variable.ttf` is the unmodified 53,096-byte
[Google Fonts COLRv1 test font](https://github.com/googlefonts/color-fonts/blob/0046ea4c3b69e9fbbe464c2594816894e3aa5e4b/fonts/test_glyphs-glyf_colr_1_variable.ttf),
revision `0046ea4c3b69e9fbbe464c2594816894e3aa5e4b`, SHA-256
`ad575a09d6748aebcb3b90ffd384c64d5c64b5fd9927967e7cd7cc0d70c98d34`.
The repository's Apache-2.0 license is copied to `LICENSE-APACHE.txt`.
The fixture contains 221 glyphs, 44 variation axes and a COLR VarStore.
[Upstream descriptions](https://github.com/googlefonts/color-fonts/blob/0046ea4c3b69e9fbbe464c2594816894e3aa5e4b/glyph_descriptions.md)
explain the paint graphs. These are test assets, not packaged UI fonts.

`skia-*.png` are independent CPU Skia reference renders, generated by
`render_references.py` with `skia-python==144.0.post2` (Skia milestone 144).
They exercise partial sweep gradients, variable sweep angles, variable clips,
two-circle radial gradients, variable radii, negative normalized radii,
variable gradient alpha, isolated SRC_IN compositing and
foreground color/paint alpha. `skia-references.json` records each codepoint,
glyph ID, design-axis value and foreground color. No Python runtime dependency
is added to Nova. Regenerate in a temporary environment:

```sh
python -m pip install skia-python==144.0.post2
python tests/fixtures/emoji/render_references.py
```

The reference canvas is transparent 128×128 RGBA, the font is 100 pixels,
origin/baseline is `(14, 114)`, hinting is disabled and subpixel positioning is
enabled. Place the CPU painter's returned bitmap at `(14 + left, 114 - top)`
before comparing. Account for antialiasing differences at boundaries; compare
premultiplied colors or ignore color differences at alpha zero. The references
are independent rasterizer evidence, not Android device screenshots or proof
that the two Skia versions produce identical antialiasing.

Useful fixture coordinates (axis indices are zero-based; normalized values are
signed F2Dot14 values passed to the CPU painter):

| Glyph | Feature | Axis | Design value | Normalized bits |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 14 (`U+F0202`) | sweep 0° to 90°, Pad | default | 0 | 0 |
| 14 | extend sweep end to 135° | `SWPE`, index 1 | 45 | 8192 |
| 160 (`U+F0C04`) | clip `[250,250,750,750]` font units | default | 0 | 0 |
| 160 | increase clip xMin from 250 to 500 | `CLXI`, index 36 | 250 | 8192 |
| 93 (`U+F0503`) | contained radial gradient | default | 0 | 0 |
| 93 | vary start radius | `GRR0`, index 16 | 250 | 4096 |
| 125 (`U+F0A05`) | SRC_IN compositing | default | 0 | 0 |
| 155 (`U+F0B07`) | foreground solid, paint alpha 0.3 | default | 0 | 0 |
| 177 (`U+F1000`) | transparent red to opaque blue | `APH2`, index 42 | -1 | -16384 |
| 93 | shift all stops below the radial cone tip | `COL1`/`COL2`/`COL3`, indices 18–20 | -1.5 each | -12288 each |

The default clip's nontransparent device bounds are `[39,39,89,89)`; the varied
clip's bounds are `[64,39,89,89)`. Interior pixel `(64,64)` is RGBA
`[143,173,143,255]` in both reference clips. The solid foreground reference uses
opaque green; the interior alpha is 76 after the font paint's 0.3 multiplier.

The negative-radius reference uses original radii 0 and 256 with stop offsets
-1.5, -1 and -0.5. Skrifa's normalized circles therefore have radii -384 and
-128, but the Pad result is opaque red over the entire 100×100 clip. Interior
pixel `(64,64)` is `[255,0,0,255]`. A shader cannot discard the fill merely
because both *normalized* radii are negative.

The alpha-gradient reference's clean midpoint `(35,54)` is straight RGBA
`[130,0,125,126]`: Skia 144 interpolates straight sRGB channels here. A tagged
sRGB surface produces the same result. This records actual native renderer
behavior; the OpenType CPAL specification instead describes premultiplied
linear-light interpolation. Keep that distinction explicit when using these
snapshots to assess cross-platform consistency.

Local validation environment: the existing ARM64 Android Skia 0.153.3 archive
contains `SkScalerContextFTUtils::drawCOLRv1Glyph`, `colrv1_traverse_paint` and
`FT_Get_Color_Glyph_Paint` symbols. `adb devices -l` found no attached device.
ImageMagick 7.1.2-31 with its FreeType delegate produced transparent output for
COLRv1 and is unsuitable as a reference. The Python Skia wheel successfully
painted the fixture in color; it supplies the checked-in reference snapshots.
